seatFocus.RAY: Trucks and trailers — hitching/backing as pinch-point work with a spotter, shop repairs under hot-work rules, rack work tied off. Standing habit: truck inspections done like trailer inspections; readiness forms on every return; rentals rig-checked 15-for-15; cascade pressures, hoses, masks counted before the line sleeps.
seatFocus.JACOB: Exxon AGT, benzene, and the breakroom conversation — pre-task discipline on every cellar entry, benzene monitor paired and logged on every air job, zeros checked out loud, and the authority to stop. Every AGT scenario worth talking about goes to the breakroom. His closing question: what did the field teach us yesterday that the breakroom should know?
seatFocus.ALEX: Equipment checks and weekend helper training — monitors calibrated, SCBA staged, windsocks up, every package checked against the layout on every route. Every weekend one 1099 or SSE rides along and learns a skill on purpose, logged as a line to Jimmy.
seatFocus.CALEB: The most spread-out team: workover · flowback · SM maintenance, days and nights across three job types — run the contact rhythm like a system.

contactRhythm: One number: every remote tech calls their Team Lead first — and the lead answers or calls back inside 30 minutes, every time.
The noon line: every scattered crew texts one line by noon — location, status, needs. No line by 12:30, the lead calls them. Silence is never 'probably fine.'
Night handoff is a call, not a text: flowback and workover changeovers happen voice-to-voice — readings, pressures, what to watch.
Breakroom to the phone: the nightly breakroom PDF goes to every remote tech.
Face time — seven-day rule: nobody goes a week without seeing their lead in person.
Friday reaches everywhere: recognition names include the remote crews — the breadth rule doesn't stop at the yard gate.
